parts.markdown:
Use our free **New Jersey paycheck calculator** to estimate your salary after federal income tax, New Jersey income tax and applicable employee payroll contributions. Enter your gross income, choose your payment schedule and customize your deductions to see your estimated take-home pay.

New Jersey employees may notice more deduction categories on their pay stubs than employees in many other states. These can include unemployment insurance, temporary disability insurance and family leave insurance.

Whether you work in Newark, Jersey City, Trenton, Princeton or another New Jersey community, understanding these deductions can help you evaluate your earnings and plan your finances.

## How to Use the NJ Paycheck Calculator

If your pay stub lists New Jersey employee payroll contributions, include the amount under other deductions. Enter each deduction once.

Choose whether you receive an annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your earnings before taxes and select your pay frequency. Common payment schedules include weekly, biweekly, semimonthly and monthly payroll.

Enter federal and New Jersey income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Enter employee benefit deductions, retirement contributions and additional withholding where relevant.

For employees approaching annual taxable wage limits, year-to-date earnings are particularly useful. New Jersey applies different limits to its unemployment, disability and family leave contributions.

Review your estimated paycheck breakdown and compare it with your employer's payroll statement.

## How New Jersey Income Tax Affects Your Paycheck

New Jersey has a progressive gross income tax system. Higher taxable income may result in portions of your earnings being subject to higher tax rates.

However, your actual payroll withholding also depends on the withholding information you provide to your employer.

The New Jersey Employee's Withholding Allowance Certificate, commonly known as Form NJ-W4, allows you to provide state-specific withholding information.

Employees with multiple jobs or households with more than one wage earner may need to adjust their withholding selections.

Additional state tax withholding can also be requested when necessary.

Review the official [NJ-W4 guidance](https://nj.gov/treasury/taxation/njit29.shtml) if your household income or employment circumstances change.

State withholding does not necessarily equal the tax you will ultimately owe on your New Jersey income tax return. Other income sources, exemptions, credits and deductions can influence the final amount.

## New Jersey Unemployment Insurance Contributions

Unlike many states, New Jersey generally requires covered employees to contribute toward its unemployment insurance system.

For standard covered workers, the 2026 unemployment insurance contribution rate is 0.3825%.

The employee taxable wage base is $44,800.

An employee who has not reached the annual limit and receives $2,000 in covered wages would contribute approximately:

$2,000 × 0.003825 = $7.65

The maximum standard annual contribution under this rate is $171.36.

Once the applicable covered wage base is reached with an employer, withholding generally stops for the remaining calendar year.

Employees may also contribute to workforce development and supplemental workforce funds, which have a combined standard rate of 0.0425% on the applicable wage base.

## New Jersey Temporary Disability Insurance

Temporary Disability Insurance provides financial support to eligible employees experiencing qualifying non-work-related disabilities.

New Jersey's standard employee TDI contribution rate for 2026 is 0.19%.

The employee taxable wage ceiling is $171,100, resulting in a maximum standard contribution of $325.09.

For $2,000 of covered earnings, the contribution is:

$2,000 × 0.0019 = $3.80

Approved private disability coverage may affect the deduction shown on your paycheck.

Visit the [New Jersey Temporary Disability and Family Leave Insurance website](https://www.nj.gov/labor/myleavebenefits/) for information about the programs and eligibility.

## New Jersey Family Leave Insurance

Family Leave Insurance provides benefits to qualifying employees during certain periods of family caregiving or bonding leave.

For 2026, the employee contribution rate is 0.23% on covered wages up to $171,100.

The maximum standard annual employee contribution is $393.53.

A paycheck containing $2,000 of covered earnings would generally produce a $4.60 family leave insurance contribution before the annual limit is reached.

Understanding these contributions is useful when comparing New Jersey salary offers with employment opportunities in states that do not collect similar employee payroll deductions.

## Federal Taxes on New Jersey Paychecks

Federal income tax withholding is calculated using your taxable earnings and Form W-4 information.

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered earnings to Social Security, subject to the 2026 annual wage ceiling of $184,500.

The standard Medicare contribution is 1.45% of covered earnings.

Higher-income employees may also encounter additional Medicare withholding at 0.9% when covered earnings paid by an employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

These federal contributions are separate from New Jersey's state insurance programs.

Review [IRS Publication 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) to learn how federal payroll taxes apply.

## Working in New Jersey and Pennsylvania

New Jersey and Pennsylvania have a reciprocal personal income tax agreement that affects employee compensation.

Under the agreement, Pennsylvania residents working in New Jersey generally do not owe New Jersey income tax on qualifying wages. Similarly, New Jersey residents working in Pennsylvania generally pay state income tax to New Jersey rather than Pennsylvania on covered compensation.

Pennsylvania residents working in New Jersey may need to submit Form NJ-165 to their employer to establish the applicable withholding treatment.

The agreement does not automatically eliminate Pennsylvania municipal wage taxes or cover every category of non-wage income.

Read New Jersey's official [Pennsylvania reciprocal income tax agreement guidance](https://nj.gov/treasury/taxation/njit25.shtml) before assuming your paycheck is exempt from a particular tax.

## Living in New Jersey and Working in New York

Many New Jersey residents commute to New York for employment.

Unlike the Pennsylvania arrangement, New Jersey and New York do not have the same reciprocal wage income tax agreement.

Depending on your circumstances, you may have tax filing responsibilities in both states. A resident tax credit may reduce double taxation on qualifying income.

Remote work arrangements can introduce additional complications involving the sourcing of employment income.

If you work across state lines, obtain a multi-state estimate rather than assuming that a New Jersey-only paycheck calculation captures every applicable tax.

## Retirement Contributions and Other Deductions

Employee benefits can substantially change New Jersey take-home income.

Traditional 401(k) contributions, Roth retirement contributions, health insurance premiums and other benefits may have different tax treatments.

New Jersey does not automatically follow every federal tax deduction or benefit provision.

For example, the state treatment of certain retirement and health-related accounts can differ from federal treatment.

Check the taxable wage amounts shown on your payroll statement and consult the [New Jersey Division of Taxation](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/) for applicable rules.

## Planning Your Monthly Budget in New Jersey

When evaluating a salary, focus on net earnings rather than gross compensation.

Consider housing, commuting, childcare, insurance and other recurring household costs.

Employees commuting to New York City or Philadelphia may face substantial transportation expenses, making disposable income more important than the advertised salary alone.

Use our [savings](/calculators/savings-calculator/) and [loan](/calculators/loan-calculator/) calculators to evaluate how much of your paycheck you can allocate toward emergency savings, debt repayment and future purchases.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why are there so many deductions on my New Jersey paycheck?

New Jersey collects employee contributions for programs including unemployment insurance, workforce development, temporary disability and family leave, in addition to ordinary federal and state taxes.

### Does New Jersey have a wage limit for disability contributions?

Yes. The standard employee taxable wage base for temporary disability and family leave insurance is $171,100 in 2026. Unemployment and workforce contributions use a separate $44,800 wage base.

### Is a New Jersey paycheck calculator accurate for New York commuters?

A New Jersey-only calculator may not capture all taxes for employees working in New York. Interstate employment can require separate withholding and resident tax credit calculations.
